meta.title: Nourra Holdings | AI data centre operator
meta.description: Nourra Holdings, headquartered in Singapore, operates AI data centres end to end: land and power, the mechanical and electrical supply chain, construction, and long-term operations and maintenance.

hero.aria: Abstract graphic: a row of rack elevations with blue squares rising from left to right, drawn from the company mark.

about.title: The firm
about.text: Nourra Holdings is an AI data centre operator headquartered in Singapore. We take a facility through its whole life: securing land and power, integrating the mechanical and electrical supply chain, building it, and running and maintaining it over the long term.

items.name: Site and power
items.text: We source powered buildings and developable land, and check zoning, floor loading, power capacity, permits and power-on dates.

items.name: Development
items.text: Mainly small and mid-sized AI data centres of a few megawatts, expandable in phases and handed over ready for hardware to be racked.

items.name: Supply chain
items.text: Power distribution, liquid cooling and prefabricated modules procured, integrated and delivered as one package, combining manufacturing in China with local production.

items.name: Engineering
items.text: Our own crews deliver electrical and low-voltage works, cabling, racking and facility conversion, and join larger projects as a specialist subcontractor.

items.name: Operations and maintenance
items.text: On-site teams run day-to-day operations, inspections and fault response, and handle scheduled servicing, repair and spare parts for facility and IT equipment.

items.name: Compute
items.text: Verified GPU capacity and enterprise cloud for our partners, deployed in our own facilities.

chain.title: Value chain
chain.lead: Ten layers sit between a unit of electricity and a single model call.
chain.hint: Open each layer to see what it is and where Nourra sits.

layers.name: Models and applications
layers.d: Model training, inference services and enterprise AI applications. They decide how much compute is needed, where, and when.
layers.r: The layer our clients and partners work in.

layers.name: Compute services and cloud
layers.d: Hardware turned into something you can rent: bare metal, GPU cloud, and model APIs billed by usage.
layers.r: We arrange verified GPU capacity and enterprise cloud for partners.

layers.name: Operations
layers.d: Life after go-live: staffing, inspections and fault response, plus scheduled servicing, repair and spare parts for both facility and IT equipment. Availability is defended at this layer.
layers.r: Our own on-site teams run operations and maintenance against a service level agreement.

layers.name: Cluster deployment
layers.d: Racking, cabling, power-up and commissioning once hardware arrives. A GPU cluster has thousands of cables, and one wrong run means rework.
layers.r: Our own engineering crews rack, cable and commission.

layers.name: Networking and storage
layers.d: The high-speed fabric that makes hundreds of servers behave as one machine, and the storage that holds training data.
layers.r: Specialist engineers are assigned per project and named in the plan.

layers.name: Chips and servers
layers.d: GPUs, servers and full-rack systems. Supply is tight and lead times are long. This is the scarcest link in the chain.
layers.r: We verify supply and lead times. Hardware goes straight into our own facilities.

layers.name: Cooling
layers.d: Carrying heat out of the rack. The newest full-rack GPU systems produce more heat than air can remove, so liquid runs directly across the chips.
layers.r: Designed and built to high-density standards in our own facilities.

layers.name: M&E equipment and prefabricated modules
layers.d: Transformers, switchgear, uninterruptible power, liquid-cooling equipment and prefabricated data hall modules. Their lead times and quality decide how soon a facility is built and how long it lasts.
layers.r: We integrate manufacturers and local production, then procure, assemble and deliver to site as one package.

layers.name: Building, mechanical and electrical
layers.d: Structure, floor loading, transformers and switchgear, uninterruptible power and fire protection. A facility’s ceiling is set here.
layers.r: We build our own data centres. Our crews handle electrical works and conversions.

layers.name: Power and land
layers.d: Substation capacity, power purchase and grid connection dates. How much power, and how soon, decides how large a facility can be and how fast it goes live.
layers.r: We source powered buildings and land, and check power capacity, permits and power-on dates.

inside.title: Inside the facility
inside.lead: An AI data centre does two things: it gets power into the rack and takes heat out.
inside.hint: Select a component to read about it.

parts.name: Grid connection
parts.d: The facility draws high-voltage power from the grid. How much capacity is available, and whether there are two independent feeds, is the first thing to confirm when choosing a site.

parts.name: Transformers
parts.d: They step high voltage down to what equipment can use. Total transformer capacity is, in practice, the ceiling of the facility.

parts.name: Uninterruptible power
parts.d: Batteries carry the load the instant the grid drops, until backup generators start. A GPU training run that loses power loses days of computation.

parts.name: Power distribution
parts.d: Power is split to every row and every rack. High-density racks need heavier busbars and a higher distribution rating.

parts.name: Racks and GPU servers
parts.d: Where the compute is. One current full-rack GPU system draws as much as a dozen or more conventional racks used to.

parts.name: Coolant distribution unit
parts.d: The heart of a liquid-cooled hall. It sends coolant to the cold plates in every server and brings the heated liquid back.

parts.name: Heat rejection
parts.d: Where the heat finally leaves the building. In a tropical climate like Singapore’s, this stage has a direct effect on the power bill.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.lead: A cluster passes six gates between site selection and go-live.

steps.d: Confirm land use, floor loading, ceiling height and available power. Until power is secured, nothing after it stands.
steps.r: Site survey, and checks on power capacity, permits and power-on dates.

steps.d: Fix rack density, the power architecture and the cooling scheme, then complete drawings and approvals.
steps.r: We organise design and coordinate approvals.

steps.d: Structural strengthening, transformers and switchgear, uninterruptible power, cooling pipework and fire protection.
steps.r: Built by our own engineering crews and accepted at milestones.

steps.d: Servers, network equipment and full-rack systems arrive on site to be unpacked, racked, cabled and powered.
steps.r: We verify supply and arrival dates. Our own crews rack and cable.

steps.d: Network connectivity, full-load running and thermal validation. Problems found here cost far less than problems found after go-live.
steps.r: We commission alongside specialist engineers and issue test records.

steps.d: The cluster is handed to its user and enters long-term operation.
steps.r: Our on-site team operates it against a service level agreement.

supply.title: Supply chain
supply.lead: How fast a facility gets built depends, as much as anything, on when the equipment arrives.
supply.hint: We procure and deliver power distribution, liquid cooling and prefabricated modules as one package.

steps.d: Rack density and site conditions set the power architecture, cooling method and module specification. The equipment list is fixed alongside the engineering drawings.
steps.r: We turn site conditions and client requirements into one complete equipment list.

steps.d: Switchgear, liquid-cooling equipment and data hall modules are built, pre-assembled and factory-tested, which cuts the work left for site.
steps.r: We integrate manufacturers in China with local production in Southeast Asia, and manage schedule and quality as one.

steps.d: Cross-border transport, customs clearance and arrival dates for heavy equipment have to line up with construction progress on site.
steps.r: We coordinate shipping and arrival sequence, under applicable trade and export control rules.

steps.d: Modules are set in place, connected to power and pipework, and commissioned with the rest of the facility.
steps.r: Installed by our own engineering crews and commissioned together with the manufacturer.

steps.d: Scheduled servicing, repair and spare parts once the equipment is in operation.
steps.r: We set up spares stock and a maintenance plan, carried out by the on-site team.
